solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nose cone briefly splitting and breaking in next to no time!

indicators.note: the shortened nose cone splits the word and, sitting between its letters
breaking in here means smashing up, so the assembled letters are rearranged
briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the cone phrase is dropped

parts.note: the pointed front of a rocket, taken as written

explanation.surface: A rocket's nose cone shears off and shatters in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking in' looks like the start of the definition phrase, but it is the anagram signal; 'in next to no time' trims to 'next to no time', a noun phrase matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A billionth of a second is the standard image of an almost immeasurable instant.

clue.text: Mysterious girl with hat, cape and lamp

indicators.note: something mysterious is obscure, a hint that these letters are jumbled

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: An enigmatic young woman with a hat, cloak and lantern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a cloak beside the hat; it is the map abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A light source using an electric arc between electrodes is a powerful kind of lamp.

clue.text: Sub for Palermo finally delivered up ball with cross

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters reverse
finally takes the closing letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A substitute for the Palermo football team finally crossed the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball with cross' sounds like football; it is the jewelled sphere with a cross carried by a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal regalia include a golden sphere topped by a cross, the sovereign's globe.

clue.text: Sometime earlier in the day, first of semi finals?

parts.note: sometime means former, as in the sometime mayor, so ex
am means before noon

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of semi is used

explanation.surface: A morning sports fixture, first the semi-finals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi finals' look sporting, but 'finals' are university finals.
explanation.definitionFit: Final-year university tests are examples of formal assessments, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Dictionary one lacking interest, not quite as complex?

definitions.note: here an adjective: of the named psychological complex

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by a letter

parts.note: pale means insipid, lacking colour or interest

explanation.surface: A dull dictionary entry, not quite as complicated as it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' looks like an adjective meaning complicated; it is the noun, the Freudian complex.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's complex, a child's desire for the opposite-sex parent, is named after the Theban king, and this adjective describes it.

clue.text: Road turned north past a delta — and so did railroad

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading upwards, so the letters reverse

parts.note: ago means in the past
a means one, a single
D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A road curving north past a river delta, and a railroad ran the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'railroad' looks like a train line; it is the verb meaning force someone into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To railroad someone is to coerce them, and to dragoon is also to force by threats.

clue.text: Hit for army band?

definitions.meaning: to strike someone, typically with an open hand, as in a clip round the ear
read as arm-y, a band belonging to the arm: the wristband of a shirt sleeve

explanation.surface: Is this a slap aimed at a military band?
explanation.walkthrough: 'army band' suggests soldiers playing music; split it as arm-y band, the band at a sleeve's end.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to give a light blow; the noun is the fabric band finishing a shirt sleeve at the wrist.

clue.text: A natural habitat, maybe, different from new zoo, etc

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal's natural habitat is quite unlike a new zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different from' reads as a phrase; 'different' is the signal and 'from' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where one feels at ease is, figuratively, one's own natural habitat.

clue.text: Expert in tongue disease joining hospital department

parts.note: flu, influenza, is a disease
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A specialist in tongue disease joins the hospital's department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert in tongue disease' reads as a medical specialist; the definition stops at 'tongue', a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks a language effortlessly is articulate and expert in it.

clue.text: Crust and bacon rasher together in foil cover?

parts.note: a scab is the dry crust that forms over a wound
a bard is a thin slice of bacon tied over meat before roasting

explanation.surface: A cook wraps a crust and some bacon together in tinfoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foil' looks like kitchen tinfoil, but it is the fencing sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath holds a sword such as a fencing foil, so it is that weapon's cover.

clue.text: What was injurious to 'Ancock?

indicators.note: the comedian Tony Hancock, said as 'Ancock, drops his aitches, so the H goes from the synonym

parts.note: injurious means damaging, causing hurt

explanation.surface: A question about what harmed the comedian Tony Hancock.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hancock's famous sitcom sketch The Blood Donor he protests that a pint is 'very nearly an armful'; read whole, the clue points to that line.
explanation.definitionFit: Hancock balked at giving as much blood as an arm can hold, so that quantity is what threatened him.

clue.text: Dutch American expats may

parts.note: expatriates may long for home, that is pine for it
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: A claim about what Dutch and American people living abroad may do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' looks like the nationality; in Cockney slang 'my old Dutch' is a man's wife. The wordplay reads as a sentence: expats may miss US.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a man's wife.

clue.text: One can serve starters: seasonal food?

parts.note: spring is a season
board is food, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A menu note: starters made from seasonal food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serve starters' sounds like a restaurant; here it means acting as a launch for those starting out.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexible platform used to launch a dive is figuratively anything that gives a start to beginners.

clue.text: Extensive supporting cast

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
to found metal is to cast it in a mould, as in a foundry

explanation.surface: A theatre review praising a large supporting cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting cast' reads as one theatre phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep and thoroughgoing knowledge is far-reaching, hence wide-ranging in extent.

clue.text: Some gathered plane tickets for out-of-this-world destination

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone collects air tickets for a trip somewhere extraordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars, nicknamed for its rusty colour, is a destination literally off the Earth.

clue.text: Online dealer; as announced

indicators.note: as announced means said out loud, so the spoken name of the mark gives the letters

parts.note: a semicolon is drawn as a dot above a comma

explanation.surface: A trader working on the internet, as stated.
explanation.walkthrough: The semicolon is not punctuation here but the wordplay: a dot over a comma, and 'dot comma' spoken in a non-rhotic accent is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person running an internet business is a trader whose company has a web address.

clue.text: Legendary runner outwitted ace in Olympic venue

indicators.note: in means the ace letter goes inside the city name

parts.note: Atlanta hosted the 1996 Summer Olympics
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A famous athlete was outfoxed by an ace at an Olympic stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the swift huntress lost a race when Hippomenes dropped golden apples she stopped to pick up.
explanation.definitionFit: The huntress of Greek myth, beaten through a trick with golden apples, is a legendary sprinter who was fooled.

clue.text: Carries out hit-and-run attack: the main details

parts.note: to nut someone is to headbutt them, so he carries out that hit
bolts means makes a run for it after the attack

explanation.surface: A thug lands a blow and flees the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: To nut someone is British slang for headbutting them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the basic practical workings of something, its essential particulars.

clue.text: Large green stone beneath a plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first pieces sit beneath the word a, which comes first

parts.note: eco is environmentally friendly, green
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A large green stone underneath a plant in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Costmary, once used to flavour beer, is the herb meant here.

clue.text: Legend in game, but not going down a treat in Milan?

indicators.note: in means the reversed story goes inside the game word

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game

indicators.note: in a down clue, not going down means going up, so the word reverses

parts.note: a legend is a tale

explanation.surface: A legendary player who is not being relegated enjoys a treat in Milan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not going down' sounds like avoiding relegation; in a down clue it means the letters run upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian ice cream is a typical sweet treat in an Italian city, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Gym miles to the west of ruined Welsh castle

indicators.note: in an across clue the west is the left, so these letters come first

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
broke means financially ruined

explanation.surface: Directions to a gym a few miles west of a crumbling Welsh castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' looks like a description of the castle; it is a piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This Norman fortress in Pembrokeshire, south-west Wales, is the birthplace of Henry VII.

clue.text: Method of cooking cabbage that's caught on

indicators.note: the vegetable word holds the short word for about, as if it had caught it

parts.note: cole is an old name for cabbage, as in coleslaw
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A cabbage-based way of cooking that has become popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught on' reads as 'became popular'; split it so 'caught' signals an insertion and 'on' is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louisiana style of cooking, spicy with tomatoes and peppers, is named after its people.

clue.text: Have fewer computers to manage

parts.note: to cut is to reduce, to have fewer
IT, information technology, means computers

explanation.surface: Reduce the number of computers an office has to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a sentence: have fewer computers is cut IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to succeed or cope, as in 'he can't hack it'.

clue.text: Prophet's book, as prepared for a Mass

definitions.note: the clue reads prophet is, so a noun naming a seer

parts.note: a la, in the style of, as in a dish prepared for a particular taste

explanation.surface: A prophet's book, written as preparation for celebrating Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Testament prophet is the one whose donkey spoke to him in the Book of Numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical seer hired to curse Israel, who blessed it instead, is a prophet by name.

clue.text: Public's tune did best

parts.note: out means public, known; out's is out is
to hone is to refine or sharpen, to fine-tune

explanation.surface: A public's favourite tune came out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Public's' is read as 'public is', the short form of out is.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine brighter than rivals is to excel them, doing better than all the others.

clue.text: Which you need a head for?

definitions.text: Which you need a head for?

indicators.note: the word for which needs its head letter to be complete, so without it the head is missing

parts.note: that can mean which, as in the book that I read

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that only works if you have a head.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the synonym for 'Which' needs its first letter put back, so the answer is that word headless; read whole, you need a head to wear one.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear is worn on the head, so a head is exactly what a bonnet or cap needs.

clue.text: Backed party, of course?

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so both pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A sponsored party, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like a phrase meaning naturally; 'course' alone is the definition, a meal's course.
explanation.definitionFit: A course of a meal is an example of something to eat, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Knocking shop people ultimately thought to stop visiting repeatedly

parts.note: to shop people is to inform on them, to rat

indicators.note: the final letter stops up the run of visiting words, sitting inside it

parts.note: at means visiting, as in at the neighbours, said three times

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of thought is used

explanation.surface: An informer, thinking to halt repeated calls at a brothel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking shop' is British slang for a brothel, but 'Knocking' is the definition and 'shop people' means inform on people.
explanation.definitionFit: The repeated sound of rapping on a door is imitated by this word.
